recipes.name: Pork Stew in Green Salsa (Guisado de Puerco con Tomatillos)
ingredients_raw: 1 (3 pound) boneless pork shoulder roast, trimmed of excess fat and cut into 1-inch cubes
2 tablespoons olive oil, or more if needed
1 (7 ounce) can diced green chiles, drained
2 fresh jalapeno peppers, seeded and chopped

steps.text: Combine flour, pepper, 1 teaspoon salt, and cumin in a large bowl. Dredge pork in flour mixture until well coated.

Heat olive oil in a large, heavy pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmers. Add pork, in batches, in a single layer; brown on all sides, about 15 minutes. Transfer pork to a bowl; cover to keep warm.

Add onion to pan; cook and stir over medium heat, adding more olive oil if necessary, until translucent and beginning to brown, about 7 minutes. Return pork to pan; stir in tomatillos, water, canned chiles, 1/2 cup cilantro, jalapeños, garlic, and marjoram. Check seasoning; add 1 pinch salt, if needed. Cover and simmer over low heat, stirring occasionally, until pork tender, about 1 hour. Degrease stew before serving in bowls, garnished with sour cream and cilantro.

raw_recipe.headline: Pork Stew in Green Salsa (Guisado de Puerco con Tomatillos)
raw_recipe.description: Tender chunks of pork are seasoned, browned, and simmered with tomatillos, cilantro, and green chilies to make a rich, flavorful stew. Serve with Spanish rice and warm tortillas.

review.reviewBody: Delicious, with wonderfully complex but balanced flavors. All the ingredients and seasonings come together and mellow into something uniquely its own. I loved the ingredients that went into this stew, loved making it, and Hubs and I certainly loved eating it! As all cooks should do, I seasoned this "to taste," upping the cumin to probably a couple of teaspoons, substituting Mexican oregano for the marjoram (have never used it!), backing off on the pepper to probably a teaspoon (you can always add it but you can't take it back out!) and subbing two, fresh poblano peppers for the canned green chilies - first, because I love 'em and second, because they're easier on Hubs' sensitive innards. Wanting to make sure the meat was good and tender, I simmered this for a good hour and a half - and it WAS buttery tender. This is intensely aromatic as it cooks, letting you know that what you're in for will be well worth the wait! I served this over plain white rice, with a dollop of sour cream, but I could easily see this wrapped in a tortilla too (that will be coming up with the leftovers!)
UPDATE TO MY RECIPE: I've been substituting 1 cup chicken broth vs. the 1 cup water! YUMMM!!!

I added a few touches, and it's now on my monthley menu. 4 cloves garlic, 1 tsp. marjoram, 1 tsp. Mexican oregano, 2 tsps. cumin, made the sour cream and cilantro sprigs optional as I have dried for the stew, and served it w/ frijoles con queso (refried beans and cheese) heated, and warm flour tortillas.

Yum! I used 2lbs of pork instead of 3, chicken broth instead of water, and oregano instead of marjoram, since that's what I had on hand, didn't change the rest of the amounts called for, and the recipe came out a tiny bit tart, but the supporting flavors were perfect. The tartness is due to the tomatillos I'm sure, which I'm not used to cooking with. Still, so delicious! I will definitely make this again. I used 2 tsp cumin, and since I had a 4oz can of diced green chiles, I left a little bit of seeds in when I diced up the jalapenos. I served this on top of rice, with tortillas on the side and our leftovers will be burritos. So good! Thank you for a wonderful recipe. **Update: I made this with 2 cans of diced tomatoes, drained (instead of tomatillos) and it was delicious! Highly recommended!

Excellent recipe!! I followed the recipe except for the cumin...I added 2 tsp, and the diced green chilis...I used 2 seven oz. cans. I also used 3 chopped serranos instead of the Jalapenos. Other than that, I stuck to the recipe. It turned out amazingly well. Stir it quite often while simmering or it will stick to the bottom of your pot. Thanks for posting Plato. We will enjoy this stew over and over again.

This chili verde was just ok. I followed the recipe pretty closely but was just not blown away. My husband is mexican and he wasn't that impressed with this either. I will make this again but will use another recipe I found. Next time I make this I will roast the tomatillos and garlic and then blend it along with the cilantro. We like our food spicy and this wasn't spicy enough for us.

Very tasty Chile Verde. I used pork shoulder/butt, removed all the fat and cooked it in a dutch oven. I wound up with pork cracklings that I lightly salted. I ate them all right then and there!! I fried the pork cubes in the lard that rendered, making the pork extremely tasty since I fried it in its own fat. I used 2 cups chicken broth and half marjoram and half oregano and simmered it for 1 1/2 hours. Delicious. I will make this again.

This was a really great recipe but I did make several alterations. By following others advice, I used 3 poblano peppers and 2 jalapenos. I roasted them under the broiler with the tomatillos for a bit, and peeled them before adding to the stew. I also added a jar of HERDEZ Tomatillo Verde Mexican Cooking Sauce for more liquid and substituted chicken broth for the water.

My additions were to add a can of hominy and a can of white beans. Probably not authentic, but it really added some depth to it. Simmered for over an hour until the pork was tender and juicy. 

Served with the rice, the whole family thought it was a keeper!!

This was an awesome recipe! The only ingredient change I made was I used 2 tbsp+2 tsp dried cilantro as I didn't have fresh. 

I converted this recipe to be prepared in the Instant Pot pressure cooker. I used the saute mode to do the first two steps - brown the pork cubes in batches and then the onion. Then I put the rest in the IP, and selected the pressure cook meat/stew setting default of 35 minutes. When the timer went off, I let it natural release on the keep warm setting and it took about 20 minutes to release pressure. 

It came out extremely tender and flavorful!

My husband loved this! He said that it could easily pass for a dish at our favorite Mexican restaurant. I followed the recipe exactly, except I let the whole dish simmer in the crock pot on low for about 5 hours. The flavors combined perfectly and the meat was so tender it just melted! I served with mexican rice and warm tortillas for a great meal!

Muy Delicioso! Use 5-6 tomatillos if you likey the tomatillos (and don't wanna guess how many makes 2 cups). Plus, use the juice from the green chiles can and cut the water back to a splash (~1/4 cup).

Found this unique recipe and glad we tried it; really really good. Didn’t make any changes to the recipe. We did do one minor change to the instructions; instead of dredging the pork in the dry ingredients we sprinkled it a little at a time and tossed the meat in it till it was all mixed in. This gave a really nice, uniform coating, and when we eventually transferred the meat into the cast iron for browning, we simply tossed the remaining dry ingredients at the bottom of the bowl into the stew to simmer. Maybe it made the stew a little thicker, idk, but it worked well. Next time we will do maybe 50% more meat- that was the star. The wet ingredients of the stew, especially the tomatillo, winning best supporting role. Wondering if this will freeze well- hoping so as it would be awesome be able to just thaw it out and have such a tasty, hearty meal. Thanks for sharing this recipe!
Followed it to the letter with very good results. I can see this as great comfort food.
Made per recipe but skipped the sour cream and additional cilantro.
This is absolutely delicious. Made as written. Great eaten as a stew and also wrapped in tortillas.

I used boneless chicken thighs & legs instead of the pork, because that’s what I had. I also used green tomatoes instead of tomatillos because I picked several green tomatoes out of my garden yesterday. I also added 1/2 teaspoon coriander and I doubled the garlic. It was absolutely delicious. My husband and granddaughter loved it. I will definitely make again.

If you are looking for a spicy dish, this is not it. If you are looking for a delicious stew full of compex flavors and tender pork, this is definitely it! I used fresh poblanos instead of canned chiles and added more cumin simply because we like it. Otherwise, this recipe was amazing. I served it over Spanish rice with extra cilantro, sour cream and diced avocado. Honestly, it didn't need any toppings but the avocado really went well with it. This is definitely a keeper! And if you prefer more heat, you can also garnish with more fresh jalepeno or red chili flakes.
I was blown away by how delicious this was! It's a real 'keeper'!
This is soooo good!

My family LOVES this recipe. I have made it exactly like the recipe, but I have also changed it up a bit. It is a big hit every time. It is a favorite, unfortunately if you are cooking by yourself, this one takes a long time. My husband thinks it is worth every minute. I make quick Spanish rice to go with it. We like it without sour cream.
